title: Product value over public and executable technical knowledge

method.unit: A named product offer, not a whole-company analogy.
method.evidence: Primary licensing, billing and technical documentation. Published offers are DOCUMENTED, not observed purchases or demonstrated outcomes.
method.analysis: Buyers and value mechanisms are INFERRED; defensibility and proposed tests are HYPOTHESIS.
method.scope_limit: No product execution, buyer interviews, contracts, comparative benchmarks or feature-level revenue data were obtained.
method.license_limit: Public source, free usage, open licenses, public standards and customer-private data are distinct. Licenses are bounded to the named artifact, not its entire ecosystem.
method.source_limit: External pages are mutable retrieval snapshots, not archived raw evidence. Source locators identify the inspected sections; no current price or tier is guaranteed.
method.attributed_revenue_semantics: null means no revenue attributable to this comparison unit or mechanism was established.

cases.comparison_unit: Actions hosted execution and deployment controls

documented.substrate: MIT-licensed Actions runner; users supply workflow and build logic.
documented.commercial_layer: GitHub-hosted execution, storage and repository-integrated control plane.
documented.paid_offer: Private repository usage above included allowances is billed; standard hosted runners for public repositories and self-hosted runner usage are free under the inspected billing documentation.
documented.meter: Runner minutes and storage usage; repository owner pays. Failed runs still consume time.
documented.capability: Environment protection can gate jobs and secrets on approval; required reviewers on Free, Pro and Team are limited to public repositories.
documented.caveat: Open runner code does not license the GitHub service. Self-hosted usage being free does not make machines or operations free. One listed reviewer suffices; approval is not correctness.

analysis.buyer: Engineering/platform team already operating repositories on GitHub.
analysis.mechanism: Remove executor operations and connect code changes, permissions and review in an existing workflow.
analysis.similarity: A modernization recipe can remain public while reliable execution and review are separately supplied.
analysis.disanalogy: CI is recurrent general-purpose infrastructure, not a migration-knowledge product; billed time rewards consumption rather than accepted outcomes.
analysis.knowledge_reason: The meter applies to execution of customer-selected logic, not exclusive migration rules.
analysis.other_dependencies: Operated service, identity/repository integration and customer workflow state.

defensibility.thesis: Installed workflow and identity integration make replacement costly.
defensibility.failure: Equivalent self-hosted or competing CI plus portable workflows is cheaper after operations cost.

cases.comparison_unit: HCP Terraform resource management and governance subscriptions

documented.substrate: Terraform configurations and provider interfaces; the inspected AWS provider is MPL-2.0.
documented.commercial_layer: Shared execution, state-aware resource management, concurrency and higher-tier governance.
documented.paid_offer: Free resource allowance, Essentials pay-as-you-go and sales-led Standard/Premium plans; Premium documents audit logging and custom RBAC.
documented.meter: Managed-resource hours with monthly billing for pay-as-you-go; committed/custom contracts also documented.
documented.capability: Execution, VCS integration and private module registry are available in Free as well as paid plans.
documented.caveat: Current Terraform core license covers version 1.6.0 onward under BSL, with a competitive-use restriction and later MPL change date; it is not a clean all-OSS example. Overview prose says Free includes SSO and policy enforcement while tables withhold them; SSO tables also disagree on Essentials. Exact disputed entitlements remain unresolved and are not used as conclusions.

analysis.buyer: Platform/infra team coordinating shared infrastructure and audit requirements.
analysis.mechanism: Centralize execution and operational state across teams, with priced capacity and control.
analysis.similarity: A domain-aware control plane can add value above reusable modules or recipes.
analysis.disanalogy: Terraform manages continuing desired state and drift; one-off migration has no equivalent resource-hour recurrence. Licensing also limits competitive reuse.
analysis.knowledge_reason: Coordinating state, permission and execution does not require exclusive infrastructure recipes.
analysis.other_dependencies: Stateful commercial control plane, customer state, identity integration and maintenance.

defensibility.thesis: Operational history and team controls create durable integration value.
defensibility.failure: Native CI, alternative state/control services or open alternatives meet the same controls more cheaply.

cases.comparison_unit: Snyk Open Source analysis within paid Team/Platform offers

documented.substrate: Apache-2.0 CLI and publicly inspectable advisories; some findings originate in public databases and package repositories.
documented.commercial_layer: Dependency analysis, maintained vulnerability intelligence, fix workflows, reporting and company license policy.
documented.paid_offer: Team monthly subscription with increased test limits, Jira integration and support; Enterprise Platform prepaid credits usable across capabilities.
documented.meter: Current Enterprise rate card meters Open Source per Active Contributor per Day; Team has a monthly subscription and product limits. Do not substitute older per-developer-month pricing.
documented.capability: Dependency and indirect-dependency risk analysis with remediation/PR workflows. Snyk documents its own vulnerability research and advisory maintenance.
documented.caveat: Snyk Open Source is a product name, not a service license. Public advisories do not prove open redistribution rights or that enrichment is reproducible. Vendor accuracy claims are not measured false-positive rates.

analysis.buyer: Application-security lead purchasing organization-wide developer coverage.
analysis.mechanism: Turn changing dependency facts into prioritized, maintained developer actions.
analysis.similarity: Versioned technical knowledge plus integration can reduce repeated expert investigation.
analysis.disanalogy: Threat intelligence changes continuously and may contain differentiated research; a stable published migration rule may not.
analysis.knowledge_reason: Workflow needs no exclusive facts, but Snyk explicitly combines public inputs with proprietary research. Its incremental contribution is unmeasured.
analysis.other_dependencies: Scanning implementation, continuous curation, dependency context and developer integration.

defensibility.thesis: Timely enrichment plus low-friction fixes justifies coverage fees.
defensibility.failure: Public databases and native scanners deliver equivalent actionable accuracy; alert burden outweighs benefit.

cases.comparison_unit: SonarQube Cloud private analysis and enterprise administration

documented.substrate: Public analyzer source and inspectable analysis logic; inspected sonar-java master carries the Sonar Source-Available License, not an unrestricted OSS license.
documented.commercial_layer: Hosted private-code analysis capacity and enterprise-level administration/security.
documented.paid_offer: Free/OSS offers coexist with Team and Enterprise; larger private analysis allowances and enterprise audit logs/IP restrictions are documented.
documented.meter: Private lines-of-code allowance; Team monthly or coupon billing, Enterprise enterprise-level annual billing under one/multiyear licenses.
documented.capability: DevOps binding/import is not universally paid-only; enterprise hierarchy and audit functions are differentiated.
documented.caveat: Free OSS scanning does not establish open implementation. The billing introduction says organization-level billing for both tiers but its detailed Enterprise section says enterprise-level; this record follows the detailed section and preserves the inconsistency. Exact current contract terms were not inspected.

analysis.buyer: Engineering-quality/platform lead managing private-code review and organizational standards.
analysis.mechanism: Make repeated quality evaluation and administration accessible at organization scale.
analysis.similarity: Inspectable rules can coexist with paid evaluation capacity and governance.
analysis.disanalogy: Recurring code analysis differs from migration acceptance; static findings do not demonstrate behavioral equivalence.
analysis.knowledge_reason: Capacity and audit do not require exclusive rules, but analyzer implementation/license rights and differentiated analysis can be part of the paid value.
analysis.other_dependencies: Analyzer implementation, private code context, hosting and organizational integration.

defensibility.thesis: Consistent analysis and integrated review reduce coordination costs.
defensibility.failure: Native checks meet policy needs or low-signal gates add more review than they save.

documented.substrate: Standardized OpenTelemetry instrumentation and supported upstream-collector ingestion paths.
documented.commercial_layer: Hosted telemetry retention, correlation, visualization and alerting with service-specific features.
documented.paid_offer: Paid monitored infrastructure and custom metrics; historical metrics remain available for inactive hosts.
documented.meter: Hourly monitored host counts using the lower-99%-of-hours high-water mark; custom metric hours averaged for billing.
documented.capability: OpenTelemetry ingestion is supported; feature compatibility varies with SDK/collector choice.
documented.caveat: Open instrumentation does not make back-end features equivalent. Infrastructure billing must not be confused with incident-response seats or other product meters.

analysis.buyer: SRE/operations team responsible for live-system diagnosis.
analysis.mechanism: Operate storage/query infrastructure and correlate a customer's otherwise fragmented live telemetry.
analysis.similarity: Open inputs can feed a useful paid operational service.
analysis.disanalogy: Live observability has recurring high-volume signals. Sparse, sensitive, heterogeneous migration outcomes do not automatically yield a transferable data advantage.
analysis.knowledge_reason: Customer-specific measurements and reliable analysis are not exclusive public-domain rules.
analysis.other_dependencies: Private customer telemetry, hosted implementation and operations. Cross-customer reuse rights and learning effects are unknown.

defensibility.thesis: Operational history and integrated diagnosis make the service valuable.
defensibility.failure: Retention economics, portability limits or an adequate alternative erase its net advantage; migration data proves too sparse to generalize.

cases.comparison_unit: AWS DMS replication, schema conversion and data validation

documented.substrate: Supported database interfaces, including open-source databases; the DMS engine and conversion knowledge are not established as open by these sources.
documented.commercial_layer: Managed data movement, replication capacity, storage and supported validation.
documented.paid_offer: Replication instances/additional log storage and serverless capacity are charged; Schema Conversion itself is free, while associated S3 storage is charged.
documented.meter: Instance/serverless capacity hours and storage; homogeneous migrations are hourly without replication instances.
documented.capability: Optional validation compares corresponding source/target rows and reports mismatches; it consumes additional resources and time. Unsupported/no-primary-key/error states are distinguished.
documented.caveat: Data-row checks are not whole-application equivalence. Supported endpoints and validation states constrain coverage. No zero-data-loss guarantee was independently verified.

analysis.buyer: Database/platform migration owner with an execution deadline and data-integrity responsibility.
analysis.mechanism: Charge for operated migration capacity rather than every planning or conversion step.
analysis.similarity: Direct modernization activity with documented validation and a separated execution meter.
analysis.disanalogy: Database replication is not source-code transformation; this is not proof of a fully open knowledge substrate.
analysis.knowledge_reason: Conversion internals and exclusive knowledge contribution are not established; free conversion is not open conversion.
analysis.other_dependencies: Managed infrastructure, database adapters and customer data access.

defensibility.thesis: Cloud distribution and operated data movement support a bundled migration offer.
defensibility.failure: Native replication or specialist tools work better; cloud integration constrains choice. A downstream-cloud subsidy rationale remains inference, not disclosed economics.

cases.comparison_unit: Moderne platform/DX and private-repository CLI execution over OpenRewrite

documented.substrate: Apache-2.0 OpenRewrite core with executable recipes; this core license does not cover every recipe or Moderne component.
documented.commercial_layer: Multi-repository execution using prebuilt lossless semantic trees, repository grouping, PR/report workflow and private/air-gapped delivery options.
documented.paid_offer: Enterprise customer/private tenant path; Connector and DX require signed contracts. CLI private-repository recipe execution requires a license; public-repository usage follows an authentication path without that license requirement.
documented.meter_limit: Contract pricing basis was not established; do not infer per-seat, per-repo or outcome pricing.
documented.capability: CLI can sync recipe catalogs, download prebuilt LSTs and use organization repository groups. Documented license signature checking need not call home.
documented.caveat: Some Moderne-created analysis/transformation recipes carry a proprietary license. This is not exclusively open recipes plus hosting. Local/private delivery contradicts a requirement for centralized telemetry.

analysis.buyer: Platform/modernization lead coordinating code change across a private repository fleet.
analysis.mechanism: Amortize parsing, dependency/context collection and rollout/review coordination across repositories.
analysis.similarity: Closest comparison: reusable executable transformation knowledge beneath commercial multi-repository modernization.
analysis.disanalogy: Typed semantic trees and native recipe execution are substantial specialized implementation; licensed recipes confound a pure workflow-only argument. This is an incumbent alternative to a new package layer.
analysis.knowledge_reason: Open recipes can power execution, but the documented product also includes proprietary recipes; their relative value is unknown.
analysis.other_dependencies: Semantic implementation, customer code/context, native recipe ecosystem and execution integration.

defensibility.thesis: Accurate semantic execution and fleet coordination outperform wrappers around single-repo tools.
defensibility.failure: Native OpenRewrite plus existing CI and review performs equally well; maintenance or license costs exceed coordination savings.

cases.comparison_unit: RHEL Server Standard/Premium physical or virtual subscriptions

documented.substrate: Component-licensed software; the inspected GPLv2-based EULA preserves component rights with firmware/trademark qualifications. CentOS Stream public development sources are distinct from exact RHEL sources available through customer/partner portals.
documented.commercial_layer: Maintained release stream, patches, upgrades, lifecycle options, support and knowledge-base access.
documented.paid_offer: Software license alone supplies no maintenance, upgrade or support entitlement; subscription/service terms supply those. Self-support offerings exist outside the selected support tiers.
documented.meter: For these Server Standard/Premium offers: physical node up to two sockets or two virtual nodes per subscription; not a universal RHEL tariff.
documented.capability: Lifecycle maintenance and operational assistance are documented subscription inclusions.
documented.caveat: Exact supported-release reproducibility was not tested; public development source is not an exact release archive. Listed support is not an application-migration correctness guarantee.

analysis.buyer: Infrastructure/platform owner and enterprise procurement covering a production estate.
analysis.mechanism: Purchase continuing release engineering and accountable assistance instead of assembling and maintaining it internally.
analysis.similarity: Public recipes can coexist with paid updates, compatibility work and environment-specific support.
analysis.disanalogy: An ongoing OS estate supports subscription recurrence; application-specific migrations may be episodic and need different acceptance criteria.
analysis.knowledge_reason: Maintenance and support can be valuable without secret Linux concepts; incident expertise may differentiate but exclusivity is unverified.
analysis.other_dependencies: Sustained engineering, support delivery, compatibility testing and customer environment context.

defensibility.thesis: Maintenance continuity and credible support justify estate coverage.
defensibility.failure: Equivalent maintenance is available elsewhere or the supported lifecycle is unnecessary.

cases.comparison_unit: Unified IntelliJ IDEA free functionality versus Ultimate subscription

documented.substrate: Continued open-source build: Apache-2.0 software with third-party terms. Current build terms are distinct from the unified free/paid distribution.
documented.commercial_layer: Advanced framework-aware and integrated developer tooling within the same IDE.
documented.paid_offer: Since 2025.3 the unified distribution retains free core Java/Kotlin use and unlocks advanced Spring/JVM/data/profiling/HTTP capabilities with Ultimate. Some basic Spring and database features are free.
documented.meter_limit: Feature subscription verified; exact billing-seat terms and rates were not established.
documented.capability: Open-source build lacks some features of the free unified distribution; paid plugins require non-open licensing infrastructure.
documented.caveat: Free is not identical to open. Eligible perpetual fallback licenses still apply to older versions. No source build or productivity evaluation was executed.

analysis.buyer: Professional JVM developer or engineering organization needing advanced integrated tooling.
analysis.mechanism: Buy maintained implementation quality and interaction design over public language/framework concepts.
analysis.similarity: Public framework knowledge can support both free tools and paid integrated execution.
analysis.disanalogy: Interactive IDE features do not establish autonomous migration fidelity or an independently authoritative domain package.
analysis.knowledge_reason: Public concepts need not be secret for proprietary, high-quality implementations to differentiate.
analysis.other_dependencies: Proprietary feature implementation, integration engineering and UX; customer code is context, not a demonstrated vendor-owned moat.

defensibility.thesis: Tooling quality and workflow continuity justify premium capabilities.
defensibility.failure: Free tooling suffices; expansion of free capabilities shifts the paid boundary.

cases.comparison_unit: Artifactory self-managed Pro X/Enterprise X/Enterprise+; separate SaaS consumption boundary

documented.substrate: Package formats and basic artifact/repository operations; matrix lists OSS/JCR/CE offerings with different coverage. Current listed OSS release license/reproducibility not established.
documented.commercial_layer: Controlled artifact promotion, availability, federation, distribution and support.
documented.paid_offer: Pro X includes promotion/SLA support; Enterprise X includes HA/federation; Enterprise+ adds edge distribution/access federation. Bundled Xray capabilities are not attributed to Artifactory alone.
documented.meter: Self-managed packages include 1/3/6 Artifactory servers and minimum annual contract; additional servers purchasable. SaaS separately uses base storage-plus-transfer consumption and overage.
documented.capability: Repository caching, checksum storage, controlled promotion and multi-site availability/distribution.
documented.caveat: CE C/C++ is no-charge proprietary binary-use software, not OSS. Server entitlements are not proof of a universal per-server tariff. Do not confuse SaaS consumption with security-product contributor metrics.

analysis.buyer: Platform/DevOps team managing shared private artifacts and multi-site delivery.
analysis.mechanism: Turn package storage and promotion into a reliable organization-wide service.
analysis.similarity: Versioned outputs, controlled promotion and distribution could support modernization independently of the agent.
analysis.disanalogy: Integrity and availability of artifacts do not establish transformation correctness or behavior preservation.
analysis.knowledge_reason: Storage, promotion, replication and access controls do not require secret package-format knowledge.
analysis.other_dependencies: Proprietary implementation, operations, integrations and customer-private artifacts/permissions.

defensibility.thesis: Embedded delivery workflows and multi-site reliability justify paid infrastructure.
defensibility.failure: Simpler registries suffice or advanced governance/federation adds no customer value.

patterns.name: Fleet execution and integrated change workflow
patterns.mechanism: Reduce repeated environment/context setup and coordinate proposal, execution and review across existing repositories.
patterns.modernize_implication: Candidate product unit is an accepted fleet change, not a new knowledge-package format. Compare against incumbent native recipes plus CI before adding a layer.
patterns.limit: Paid boundaries establish an offer, not coordination savings or demand for a new entrant.

test.design: Paired same-scope fleet change using native recipe plus existing CI/review versus added coordination, with equal independent acceptance checks.
test.measure: All setup, execution, review/rework and upkeep effort per accepted repository; failure coverage; committed second use.
test.reject_if: No reduction in total accepted-change cost or no buyer for the incremental layer.

patterns.name: Scoped validation and accountable governance
patterns.mechanism: Record who authorized a change, what was checked, and what remains unresolved; enforce gates independently of generation.
patterns.modernize_implication: Separate approval authority, deterministic check coverage and evidence provenance. Buyable assurance must be scoped, not a claim of universal correctness.
patterns.limit: A signature verifies origin, an approval permits action, a row check covers data, and a static gate covers selected rules; none proves whole-application equivalence. Existing platforms may already supply governance.

test.design: Ask actual change/risk owners to evaluate identical migration results with existing controls versus an explicit acceptance/evidence record, including seeded incomplete checks.
test.measure: Review time, missed material failures, rejected unsupported claims and buyer budget ownership.
test.reject_if: Controls are redundant, added evidence increases work without improving decisions, or acceptance errors persist.

patterns.name: Maintained compatibility and accountable support
patterns.mechanism: Fund continuous compatibility/release work and human escalation rather than resell static facts.
patterns.modernize_implication: A maintained native operator and explicit support window may be more useful than a generic domain registry.
patterns.limit: Proprietary research can supplement maintenance; incident expertise and warranty liability were not measured. Episodic demand may not finance continuing upkeep.

test.design: Have an independent maintainer carry a bounded operator through two real dependency/framework changes and customer escalation.
test.measure: Upkeep and support cost, breakage discovered, customer renewal/coverage commitment.
test.reject_if: Coverage revenue cannot fund upkeep or buyers only need a one-off migration.

patterns.name: Distribution and incumbent workflow access
patterns.mechanism: Reach work where code, identities, artifacts and deployment budgets already reside.
patterns.modernize_implication: Copilot/IDE/GitHub/Azure distribution is a plausible incumbent advantage and a threat to a standalone package business, not evidence of provider-neutral authority.
patterns.limit: Distribution does not establish acquisition economics, lock-in magnitude, justified target selection or customer preference.

test.design: Offer the same bounded capability through the existing workflow and a separate interface without changing checks or target options.
test.measure: Activated and accepted changes, setup burden and procurement friction; preserve ability to choose another provider.
test.reject_if: No adoption difference or distribution requires restrictions buyers reject.

patterns.name: Hosted capacity or private managed execution
patterns.mechanism: Sell operated capacity, availability or deployment support; knowledge can remain public.
patterns.modernize_implication: Cloud execution is one delivery option; Moderne private/local licensing shows centralized collection is not mandatory. Metered consumption and successful outcomes are different units.
patterns.limit: Operations cost money and may be commoditized. Free conversion beside paid migration capacity challenges standalone planning fees; it does not reveal a provider's subsidy economics.

test.design: Cost an actual repeat workload in existing CI, managed execution and customer-controlled delivery including failures and support.
test.measure: Total cost, capacity reliability, data constraints and price a budget owner will approve.
test.reject_if: No net operational advantage or viable margin at the required deployment model.

patterns.name: Curated intelligence where incremental quality is real
patterns.mechanism: Differentiated research, analyzers or recipes may improve actionable coverage beyond public facts.
patterns.modernize_implication: Reject the absolute claim that durable value cannot live in knowledge. Measure proprietary enrichment separately from better software and workflow.
patterns.limit: Exclusive knowledge contribution is unknown; visible source or public advisory does not establish unrestricted reuse or quality superiority.

test.design: Ablate proprietary enrichment while holding workflow, context, execution and independent acceptance checks constant.
test.measure: Additional accepted cases, false positives, review cost, maintenance and license cost.
test.reject_if: Public knowledge/native implementation achieves equivalent net results.

patterns.name: Customer-specific operational history, not an assumed data flywheel
patterns.mechanism: Within-customer history and context can aid diagnosis and reproducibility; cross-customer learning is a separate unverified proposition.
patterns.modernize_implication: Preserve consent, tenant isolation, provenance and explicit reuse rights. Private code/context is not vendor-owned domain truth.
patterns.limit: No inspected source establishes migration-data learning lift, reuse permission or network effects. Datadog recurrence is the weakest analogy to episodic modernization.

test.design: Only with explicit permission, evaluate held-out migration outcomes with and without prior-run context, separating same-organization from cross-organization transfer.
test.measure: Incremental acceptance/review improvement, data freshness, coverage, privacy and curation cost.
test.reject_if: No transferable lift or insufficient lawful, representative data; retain local evidence only.

prioritization.basis: Priority for a narrow Modernize-adjacent test: direct task similarity, documented paid boundary, measurable incremental outcome and independence from unavailable data. Not estimated market size or measured moat.
prioritization.thesis_changing_implication: A maintained native operator plus accepted-change execution/evidence may be the useful unit. The portfolio does not justify a new package format, a standalone market or the elimination of differentiated knowledge as a source of value.

aggregate_revenue_evidence.limitation: Company-reported aggregate revenue confirms an operating commercial business, not revenue attributable to OTel, infrastructure observability, governance or a proprietary-data advantage.
